articles.title: India bonds gain as RBI FX inflows lift liquidity, spur short-term debt buying
articles.content: Indian government bonds saw gains early Thursday, led by shorter-term debt. Larger dollar inflows boosted rupee liquidity and improved sentiment for Indian assets. Banks raised significant foreign currency, adding to domestic liquidity for several years. This influx strengthened India's ability to support the rupee and domestic markets. Elevated oil prices and US Treasury yields continued to weigh on longer-dated bonds.

articles.title: Nominal GDP growth set to surge to 12%. Why the stock market may still struggle to rally
articles.content: India’s nominal GDP growth could accelerate to 11.5%-12% in FY27, supporting stronger corporate earnings. However, elevated valuations, rising equity supply and potentially slower domestic flows could limit broad market gains. Jefferies favours lenders, power, ports and real estate, but sees a selective stock-picking environment rather than a broad-based rally.

articles.title: IFCI shares rally over 16% in two days as NSE IPO draws closer
articles.content: IFCI shares rallied over 16% in two sessions amid expectations that the long-delayed NSE IPO could be nearing launch. articles.title: Trump’s second-term policies put US finances under growing strain as debt tops $40 trillion
articles.content: During President Trump's presidency, the national debt of the U.S. has ballooned to over forty trillion dollars. Federal expenditures are on a relentless rise, and interest on loans is climbing steeply. The tax reductions implemented by his administration have multiplied the national debt by trillions. This fiscal decline has roots that stretch back well before Trump, influenced by initiatives from both parties.

articles.title: India’s ‘real feel GDP’ growing only at 2-3%; Shankar Sharma joins the debate
articles.content: Stock market veteran Shankar Sharma has questioned India’s headline GDP growth, arguing that the economy’s “Real Feel” growth is only 2-3%. articles.title: US Market: Tech stocks challenge Wall Street’s traditional bear market definition
articles.content: The traditional 20% threshold for defining a bear market is facing fresh scrutiny as highly volatile technology and semiconductor indexes remain sharply higher for the year despite entering bear-market territory. The SOX and KOSPI have revived debate over whether factors such as volatility, duration and economic conditions should complement the conventional measure.

articles.title: Rupee gains to 94.27 vs USD as RBI measures bring in bumper $136 billion
articles.content: India's rupee has seen a remarkable increase following a significant capital boost from the Reserve Bank of India, which successfully raised over 136 billion dollars through its specialized programs. This substantial financial inflow empowers the central bank to robustly guard the rupee. Consequently, the rupee has emerged as the second-best currency performer in Asia over the last month, a response to recent outflows aimed at bolstering its value.

articles.title: Gold prices rise 2,300/10 gram in 2 days; silver gains Rs 3,300/kg as yields, dollar soften. Key levels to watch
articles.content: Gold and silver prices rose for a second straight session on MCX as the US dollar weakened and bond yields eased. Investors now await US nonfarm payrolls data for clues on the Federal Reserve’s policy path. Gold remains supported by softer yields and geopolitical tensions, while traders monitor key technical levels and domestic physical gold prices across major cities.
